subject: Order form: upfront crediting, invoicing path & tax residency checklist

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood-inference.com>

Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood-inference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Order form: upfront crediting, invoicing path & tax residency checklist

Hi Claudia —

Thanks again for the careful read of the Order Form during last week's call. I attached a refreshed version (Aurelia_OrderForm_v3.pdf) that reflects the pricing ladder we discussed and a short invoice flow diagram. A few open items surfaced on our side and I want to align on next steps so Procurement and Finance can close this week: 

- Upfront crediting: you asked whether the initial credit (annual prepay) can be applied across entities — Redwood can accept an upfront credit applied to the master payee only, but we can split invoicing across Aurelia entities if you provide entity-level PO numbers. Need confirmation on preferred approach.
- Minimum commit phasing: the schedule in Section 2 shows a staircase (Q1 40%, Q2 30%, Q3 30%). We can make the Q1 tranche refundable if you require a service-credit fallback — that would require an amendment to the Order Form.
- Net terms: default 30 days, Finance indicated a potential Net45 for large public health customers; we need a PO to route Net45 approval.
- Tax residency / withholding: if Aurelia requests withholding, we'll need local tax registration evidence and the billing entity to populate W-8/W-9 equivalents.

Can you confirm who at Aurelia will own entity PO assignment vs. tax evidence? If helpful, we can run a short call with our billing ops and Kimberly (cc'ed) to map the invoice routing and minimize tax friction.

Next step propose: 30-minute call tomorrow (Tue) 10:00am PT to walk the updated OF and identify any redlines you plan to send back. If that doesn't work, send a redline PDF and we'll have legal respond.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood-inference.com | +1 (415) 555-0198

Attachment: Aurelia_OrderForm_v3.pdf (pdf)

Date: Mon, 29 Nov 2026 12:03:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Order form: upfront crediting, invoicing path & tax residency checklist

Hi Jonas —

Thanks for the update and the PDF. Quick answers from Procurement: 

- Entity PO assignment: Procurement will provide entity-level POs for invoice splitting — I'll send the list by EOD Tue.
- Upfront credit: we prefer the prepay to be credited pro-rata across entities automatically rather than manual allocation. Is that a supported flow on Redwood's side? If not, we need clear invoice-level notes so our accounting team can reconcile.
- Net terms: Aurelia's standard is Net45 for new enterprise vendors; Finance will need Redwood's W-9 and global tax residency statement.

We'll avoid a call for now — please send the MSA redline and any proposed amendment language for refundable Q1 tranche and invoice routing. Procurement will push redlines back into DocuSign if acceptable.

Regards,
Claudia Vazquez
Senior Procurement Manager | Aurelia Health
claudia.vazquez@aurelia-health.com

Date: Tue, 30 Nov 2026 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Order form: upfront crediting, invoicing path & tax residency checklist

Claudia —

Good notes, thanks. Two quick clarifications from our side: 

1) Automatic pro-rata crediting: our billing system does not currently support a single prepay that auto-apportions across separate legal entities at invoice time. The most practical approach today is: Redwood issues the invoice(s) to the specified payee entities with clear invoice memos referencing the single upfront credit (we'll attach a credit memo per entity). That keeps your AP reconciliations straightforward while honoring the single prepay amount.

2) Net45 approval: understood. I'll escalate to Finance and include the W-9 / tax residency packet. Kimberly, can you attach the standard W-9 and a short note about withholding responsibilities? Ben, FYI on refundable tranche language — can Legal draft two alternatives (service-credit vs. refund) so Aurelia can pick?

I'll also attach a tracked MSA redline (MSA_redline_jw-kk-bc.docx) and a short amendment paragraph to slot into the Order Form for the refundable Q1 tranche. If you prefer DocuSign routing, send the HubSpot deal id and procurement contact and we can prepare the envelope.

Thanks,
Jonas

Attachment: MSA_redline_jw-kk-bc.docx (docx)
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood-inference.com>

Date: Wed, 1 Dec 2026 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: Aurelia redline strategy (billing + tax)

Ben / Jonas —

Putting notes here for Legal/Billing handoff: 

- W-9 & tax packet: attaching the standard W-9 and the global tax residency checklist. Finance needs Aurelia's entity list + country of registration to determine withholding exposure.
- Refund vs service-credit: we drafted two amendment snippets in the MSA redline. Recommendation: default to service-credit tied to uptime SLA (less back-office churn) and offer refund only if Aurelia explicitly requests cash refund (longer procurement cycle).
- Invoicing path: we'll issue entity-level invoices but include a single credit memo record (credit memos named with the single prepay and reference number). Operations team will need the PO mapping CSV (Procurement to provide).

Action items:
1) Ben: confirm Legal can deliver redline comments by EOD Thu.
2) Jonas: ask Aurelia for the PO mapping and the primary ap@ email for DocuSign routing.

Kimberly Park
Head of Billing Ops | Redwood Inference
